items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1957-03-26
items.q: him and Manuel Marlowe, in fact, were the first two kids that I picked up on horn.

ctx.x: Was Vega a ragtime player or what did you

read on it? Oh, very good ragtime player. Very good. Very good. Yeah. In fact, as I'm telling you, well, him and Manuel Marlowe, in fact, were the first two kids that I picked up on horn. Then I began to get my boy, my boy, practicing and wanting it on this fellow, Mead and Perkins, pulled him through. And then got Johnny Lawler and boys like that in another place. Well, Brunus and all, they used to be with me all the time, the Brunus boys. The Brunus boys, especially Georgie Brunus, Georgie Brunus never left my…
Did they play regular cornets in those days or were they different?

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: Manuel Marlowe, Leo Marlowe, Robbie Kirsch, Martin Kirsch, Gussie Zinneman, and the Chinaman

ctx.x: Let me get everything. Right. Papa, who was in your band when you got married about that time? Who was in your band when you got married? When I got married? Mm-hmm.
Manuel Marlowe, Leo Marlowe, Robbie Kirsch, Martin Kirsch, Gussie Zinneman, and the Chinaman, and... Was that King Martin? Yeah. Kit Martin, Vega, Buck A., and the Shields.
So many of them. I couldn't remember. Yeah. Well, do you remember when Dave Hennessy got killed? He was the chief of police? Oh, yes.
